## Design decisions (this row's)

- **Two renderers, one document.** The lane job emits its own zero-JS
  HTML (J3's no-Astro-rebuild mechanism) while `web/` renders the same
  `sig.status-lane/1` doc for the release copy of `/status/` +
  `/status/sources/` — drift is bounded because both consume the one
  document the job emits.
- **A third allow-list.** `ops/public_routes_status.toml` scopes the
  lane's publish to exactly `status/` (the P34.10 assertion pattern);
  `status/archive/**` is never deleted.
- **`freshness_verdict(include_next_fire=True)`** — the one shared
  verdict function evaluated at `status_time`; release-bound emitters
  never set the flag (the two-clock rule is structural).
- **Issue classes fold the verdict.** `late`/`overdue`/`never_run` join
  the run-derived classes so a source with zero executions still reports
  `never_run` (J3 §7.3's closed vocabulary; the curated log is TX-06's).
- **The script mirrors `flock-share-lists.sh`/`search-v2-roll.sh`:** check
  mode prints the verbatim leg offline; apply is window + ADC + env
  gated → exit 42 `QUEUED` + the verbatim re-run prompt.
